title: The Man Who Jumped Out of a Plane With $200,000
sources: Wikipedia, 'D. B. Cooper': Nov 24 1971, Northwest Orient Flight 305, Boeing 727, Portland to Seattle; FBI suspended active investigation July 2016
Biography.com: called himself Dan Cooper, paid $18.52 cash for a one-way ticket; plane then took off for Mexico City
History.com: handed flight attendant a note 'I have a bomb in my briefcase'; demanded $200,000 and four parachutes
The Week: landed Seattle 5:40 pm, released the 36 passengers
Britannica: lowered the rear steps and jumped around 8 pm, near Ariel, Washington
HistoryLink: dark and stormy Thanksgiving Eve; 'D. B.' was a reporter's mistake
HistoryLink / KIRO7: Feb 10 1980, 8-year-old Brian Ingram found $5,800 of ransom money on Tena Bar, Columbia River
Biography.com: hundreds of suspects considered, hijacker never identified

lines.text: In November 1971, a calm man in a suit bought a plane ticket for eighteen dollars,
lines.caps: In | November | 1971,~nineteen | a calm | man | in a suit | bought | a plane | ticket | for | $18~eighteen | dollars,

lines.text: under the name Dan Cooper.
Right after takeoff, he handed the flight attendant a note:
I have a bomb in my briefcase.
He wanted two hundred thousand dollars,
and four parachutes.
In Seattle, he got them,
let all thirty-six passengers go,
and told the pilots to fly to Mexico.
But somewhere over the dark, rainy forests of Washington,
he lowered the back stairs of the jet,
and jumped out into the night.
He was never seen again.
The FBI searched for forty-five years,
checked hundreds of suspects,
and found almost nothing,
except one thing:
in 1980, an eight-year-old boy digging by a river
lines.caps: in | 1980,~nineteen | an | 8-year-old~eight-year-old | boy | digging | by a | river

lines.text: found five thousand eight hundred dollars of the ransom money.
The rest of the money? Still missing.
So did D.B. Cooper die that night,
lines.caps: So | did | D.B. Cooper~d | die | that | night,

lines.text: or get away with the perfect crime?
